lines.trans: How could you forget your handbag?
Apparently, pregnancy badly impairs memory.
For heaven's sake, forgive me! Are you all right?
Give me five grand, and no hard feelings.
Wait, maybe I should take you to the hospital?
It feels like you are not moving, but running away.
Could you at least have packed your things properly?
And when you left Mom, did you pack your things properly?
No need to help, I already called a taxi.
What? Are you heading to a bar?

examples.text: Помогать не надо, я уже такси вызвала.
examples.trans: No need to help, I already called a taxi.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'taxi' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы отвратительный директор, если нанимаете таких людей.
examples.trans: You are a terrible director if you hire such people.

examples.text: Так, и моя очередь.
examples.trans: Right, and now it is my turn.

examples.text: Ничего, страшно было? Нет, там такие подушки.
examples.trans: Well, was it scary? No, there are such airbags there.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'called', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Помогать не надо, я уже такси вызвала.
examples.trans: No need to help, I already called a taxi.

examples.text: Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You called a sober driver!

examples.text: Мы сразу вызвали скорую помощь.
examples.trans: We immediately called an ambulance.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что? В бар собираетесь?
examples.trans: What? Are you heading to a bar?

examples.text: Наш бар закрывается.
examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to intend, to be about to; to gather', paired with 'собраться'.

examples.text: Я переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: I am planning to move.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

examples.text: Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Элементарно! Пришла утром, значит, не работает.
examples.trans: Elementary! She came in the morning, which means she doesn't work.

examples.text: Значит, не хочешь по-хорошему?
examples.trans: So you don't want to do this the easy way?

examples.text: Значит, ты не придёшь?
examples.trans: So you're not coming?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Привет, Лёва. Чего хотел?
examples.trans: Hi, Lyova. What did you want?

examples.text: Я хочу кофе.
examples.trans: I want coffee.

examples.text: Не хочешь, как хочешь.
examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-хорошему').

examples.text: Значит, не хочешь по-хорошему?
examples.trans: So you don't want to do this the easy way?

examples.text: Не хочешь по-хорошему.
examples.trans: If you don't want it the easy way.

examples.text: Давай договоримся по-хорошему.
examples.trans: Let's agree amicably.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно. В конце концов, ребёнок не виноват.
examples.trans: Fine. After all, the child is not at fault.

examples.text: Ладно, хорошо. Сейчас приеду.
examples.trans: Fine, all right. I will come over now.

examples.text: Ладно, не хочешь хорошего, включу плохого.
examples.trans: Fine, if you don't want the good father, I will turn on the bad one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Ладно, хорошо. Сейчас приеду.
examples.trans: Fine, all right. I will come over now.

examples.text: Значит, не хочешь по-хорошему?
examples.trans: So you don't want to do this the easy way?

examples.text: Ладно, не хочешь хорошего, включу плохого.
examples.trans: Fine, if you don't want the good father, I will turn on the bad one.

meanings.en: to switch on, to plug in
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will turn on', paired with 'включать'.

examples.text: Сейчас включу.
examples.trans: I'll plug it in right now.

examples.text: Включи, пожалуйста, чайник.
examples.trans: Switch on the kettle, please.

examples.text: Сейчас включу. Он у нас быстро всё вспомнит.
examples.trans: I'll plug it in right now. He'll remember everything quickly with us.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Ладно, не хочешь хорошего, включу плохого.
examples.trans: Fine, if you don't want the good father, I will turn on the bad one.

examples.text: И всё-таки я не верю в приметы, особенно в плохие.
examples.trans: And still I do not believe in omens, especially bad ones.

examples.text: Плохая погода.
examples.trans: Bad weather.
